title: Streams, templates and exceptions
subtitle: Generic code that works for any type, input/output as flowing streams, and errors that jump to where they can be handled.

stream.title: Streams
stream.body: A stream is a sequence of characters flowing between a program and a device. cin (input), cout (output), cerr (errors). << inserts, >> extracts, and both chain. The stream classes form a hierarchy: ios → istream/ostream → ifstream/ofstream (files) and stringstream (strings).

fmt.title: Formatting and file I/O
fmt.body: Manipulators format output: setw(6) width, setprecision(2) with fixed, endl newline-and-flush. Files: ofstream f("a.txt"); f << 42; — the destructor closes it (RAII). Check if (!f) after opening.

tmpl.title: Function templates
tmpl.body: template <typename T> T maxOf(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; } is a recipe; when you call maxOf(3, 9) the compiler instantiates a version with T = int, and maxOf(2.5, 1.5) another with T = double. One source, many type-specific functions, all checked at compile time with no run-time cost. The type must support the operations used (here >).

ctmpl.title: Class templates and the STL
ctmpl.body: template <class T> class Stack { T data[100]; int top; … }; gives Stack<int>, Stack<string>. The Standard Template Library supplies containers (vector, list, map, set), iterators and algorithms (sort, find) all built from templates.
ctmpl.steps: vector<int> v = {5, 2, 9}; sort(v.begin(), v.end()); Result order.

exc.title: Exceptions: throw, try, catch
exc.body: When a function cannot continue, it throws an object. The runtime unwinds the call stack, destroying locals on the way, until it finds a matching catch. If none is found the program terminates. try { risky(); } catch (const runtime_error& e) { … }. Use exceptions for exceptional conditions, not ordinary control flow.

safe.title: Exception safety
safe.body: Acquire resources in objects whose destructors release them (RAII, smart pointers) and exceptions cannot leak. Catch by const&, order handlers from most specific to most general, catch (...) catches anything, and never throw from a destructor. Levels of guarantee: basic (no leak), strong (all-or-nothing), no-throw.
safe.steps: Order catch blocks: derived exception types before their base. catch (const base&) first would swallow every derived type, hiding the specific handlers.
